abstract: Analysis of S&P 500 earnings call transcripts from September-December 2025 shows 'AI' was cited on 306 calls, the highest in 10 years, surpassing the previous record of 292 in Q2 2025. Companies mentioning AI outperformed peers by 8.2 percentage points on average since year-end 2024, while mentions of 'uncertainty' declined significantly from 415 in Q1 to 201 in Q3 2025. Despite CEO focus on AI investment, a survey of U.S. CFOs reveals that while 66% expect significant AI ROI within two years, only 14% report meaningful value today, hampered by data trust issues, legacy system constraints, and skills shortages.
keyFindings: The term 'AI' was cited on 306 S&P 500 earnings calls from September 15 through December 4, 2025, the highest number in at least 10 years and significantly above the five-year average of 136 and 10-year average of 86.

S&P 500 companies mentioning 'AI' on Q3 2025 earnings calls experienced higher average stock price increases than non-mentioning peers since December 31, 2024 (13.9% vs. 5.7%), June 30, 2025 (8.1% vs. 3.9%), and September 30, 2025 (1.0% vs. 0.3%).
Information technology (95%) and communication services (95%) sectors have the highest percentages of earnings calls citing 'AI' in Q3 2025.
Mentions of 'uncertainty' in S&P 500 earnings calls declined from 415 in Q1 2025 to 282 in Q2 and 201 in Q3, following Trump's 'Liberation Day' announcement.

Among 200 U.S. CFOs surveyed at enterprises with more than $500 million in annual revenue, 66% expect significant AI ROI within two years, but only 14% report meaningful value today, with 86% citing legacy systems as limiting AI readiness and only 10% fully trusting enterprise data.
methodology: FactSet analyzed S&P 500 company earnings call transcripts from September 15 through December 4, 2025, using term frequency analysis for 'AI' and 'uncertainty' mentions. Historical comparisons span 10-year period (2015-2025) with quarterly breakdowns. RGP professional services firm conducted a separate survey of 200 U.S. CFOs at enterprises exceeding $500 million annual revenue across technology, health care, financial services, and CPG/retail sectors. Stock price performance data tracked from December 31, 2024 through September 30, 2025.
qualifiers: FactSet analysis limited to S&P 500 companies with earnings calls during specified period (September 15-December 4, 2025). RGP CFO survey based on 200 respondents at enterprises with more than $500 million annual revenue; sector representation and geographic scope (U.S. only) limit generalizability. Forward-looking expectations (66% expecting AI ROI within two years) are subject to uncertainty. Stock performance correlation with AI mentions does not establish causation. Analysis does not isolate workforce-specific AI impact; broader business applications included in earnings call citations.
